1.why: Relevance item; D ties the sentence to the buyers' action described in the paragraph. B asserts a later auctioneer detail I cannot verify; C claims it is never revisited, also unverifiable.

2.why: Nonrestrictive clause needs paired commas; every other option drops one or both.

3.why: Past perfect needs participle 'gone'; 'has gone' breaks tense, progressive is unidiomatic.

4.why: Original is a comma splice; period fixes it. B makes a fragment after the semicolon, D is a run-on.

5.why: Colon introducing an appositive definition is correct; A and C leave a fragment, D is a comma splice.

6.why: 'Another patroller' is singular, so singular possessive patroller's.

7.why: Relative clause combines cleanly; B is a comma splice, D says the beans were built from wheels.

8.why: Dangling modifier: the tardigrades were dried and sealed, so they must follow the comma.

9.why: 'With nothing to look at' is an introductory phrase, needs a comma, not a period/semicolon/conjunction.

10.why: Nonrestrictive clause with paired commas is already correct.

11.why: 'The money would have to come from somewhere' reads as a concession to an objection, not an example, restatement or parallel.

12.why: Only B matches 'new form of transportation' (railroads) producing a lasting timekeeping change; A shifts to the telegraph, C/D argue against an otherwise well-fitting purpose.
